title: Inference worker GC oscillation causing intermittent throughput collapse
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
During a production capacity burst on 2026-02-17 we observed repeated short-duration throughput collapses on a subset of inference workers serving r7-small instances. Symptoms were sharp drops in tokens/sec (~60-80%) for 10-90s windows and elevated p99/p999 latencies. The incidents correlated with large numbers of kernel-selection events and KV-cache churn across concurrent requests.

Why this ticket exists:
This ticket consolidates the follow-up work from the incident retro: a recurring GC/heap-pressure oscillation in the inference worker process caused by interactions between the scheduler's aggressive preemption window and the kernel-selection metadata retention logic. The goal is to land fixes, add guardrails, and harden tests and observability so similar regressions cannot silently reoccur.

Key hypothesis (root cause):
1) Scheduler change (rolled in runtime-1.23) introduced fast preemption slices to reduce tail latency under heavy bursty load. In practice, preemption repeatedly forced short-lived kernel swaps which allocated transient kernel descriptors and per-request metadata.
2) Kernel-selection path retained references to model-specific descriptor objects longer than necessary; combined with repeated preemption this produced periodic heap fragmentation and GC cycles in the worker process.
3) The KV-cache eviction logic responded to the same churn by aggressively reclaiming prefix entries, leading to cache warmup storms and additional allocations.
4) End result: feedback loop where preemption -> allocation spike -> GC pause -> request backlog -> scheduler reacts with more preemption.

Impact observed:
- Affected ~7% of workers in the low-latency pool for ~3 hours during the incident window.
- Median tokens/sec per-worker dropped 62% during collapse windows; p99 latency increased from 210ms to ~1.4s.
- Several customer endpoints experienced elevated request timeouts and automatic fallbacks to cheaper model variants.

Repro status and diagnostics:
- Repro: synthetic stress harness reproduces oscillation when simulating 20% variability in request sequence lengths with concurrent quantized+float kernel selection. See repro harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/tree/main/diagnostics/gc-oscillation-harness
- Heap traces and flamegraphs attached in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/GC+oscillation+investigation
- Worker-level metrics: gc.pause_ms, heap.live_bytes, kernel.alloc_rate, kvcache.evict_rate added to dashboard.

Review feedback so far:
- PM (Ling Chen): prioritize a safe fast rollback toggle for the scheduler preemption change and add rollout gates.
- Design (Maya Singh): confirm telemetry required for UI alerting and color-coded severity.
- SRE (Owen Parker): request an emergency autoscaling tweak to avoid pressure on the low-latency pool while fixes are validated.

Decisions made:
- Immediate mitigation: gate the aggressive preemption behind a feature flag and roll to 10% of traffic while root-cause patches land. (rolled back to 0% on 2026-02-18 08:20 UTC)
- Short-term patch: free kernel-selection descriptors earlier by introducing explicit Reset() path after selection and reduce retention window for kernel metadata to one request.
- Medium-term: decouple KV-cache eviction from instantaneous kernel alloc rate; use smoothed eviction velocity and a hysteresis window.

Acceptance criteria for closure (high level):
- The synthetic harness shows no >20% throughput degradation across 1h runs with high-variance sequences.
- Production canary (5% traffic) runs for 72h with no GC oscillation triggers and stable p99 latencies.
- New metrics and alerts deployed; runbook updated with clear mitigations and rollback steps.
- Two reviewers sign off on code changes and canary rollout plan.
